general_information.Description: - Description: This course explores beverage service within the hospitality industry, encompassing a wide range of products - from alcoholic beverages such as spirits, wines, beers, and cocktails to non-alcoholic offerings including tea and coffee.Students will explore the development of the beverage industry, responsible alcohol service, and key product knowledge across different beverage categories. The course also introduces essential aspects of bar operations, including bar setup and equipment, basic business considerations, and service techniques for various beverages. Emphasis is placed on both theoretical understanding and practical application to support professional service performance in hospitality settings. - Teaching method: Lecture, discussion, demonstration, role-play, and group work. - Facilities and Equipment Requirement: Depending on the training conditions of each campus, the course may be delivered in simulation labs designed to meet 4–5-star hotel standards, in real hotel environments, or other appropriate training facilities that fully meet operational requirements.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Develop general knowledge on the origins and development of the beverage industry.
Develop a sense of good discipline, responsibility, cooperation, patience, carefulness and aesthetic values in the individual work as well as with colleagues.
Indicate the effects of alcohol in the human body, both positive and negative, from health claims to the latest hangover research.
Develop an overall concept and tailor it to meet the needs and desires of a particular clientele.
Identify and distinguish types of glassware, mixing tools and equipment specifications and uses
Distinguish between fermented and distilled beverages and identify them on your shelves.
Classify wines according to type and recognize some of their distinguishing characteristics.
Prepare and pratice opening techniques of wine bottle and wine service techniques.
Outline the origins of beer and the market trends affecting today’s brewing industry.
Understand the origins of tea, coffee, as well as the production and preparation of these beverages.

assessments.Question Type: Each student shoud make at least 1 individual presentation, case analysis during the course in front of the class. Topics will be varied based on the topics in the textbook.
assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.Question Type: Four or five students per group. Groups and groups ideas are determined on the third session of the course. Work will be break down into stages and examined during the course. Final work to be submitted prior to the presentation of the topic.
assessments.No Question: Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units
assessments.Note: All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 13-point font, and must be submitted in soft copy. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission Evaluation will be based on both presentation and written report (reccommded 30%, 70% accordingly)

assessments.Question Type: Four or five students per group. Competency is to be demonstrated by effectively preparing and serving beverage in accordance with the performance criteria and the range listed within the practical learning sessions.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Note: Competency in this unit may be assessed through: Demonstration of skills on mixing different (in quantity) international alcoholic beverages in a prescribed timeframe; utilizing systematic liquor pouring and proper bar measurement; mixing of alcoholic concoction showmanship skill techniques. The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.Question Type: Each student must be assessed through practical demonstration in a simulated workplace environment where beverage ingredients and equipment are provided. Competency is to be demonstrated by effectively preparing and serving beverage in accordance with the performance criteria and the range listed within the practical learning sessions.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on the practical learning sessions of the course.
assessments.Note: Competency in this unit may be assessed through: - Observation shall be done on the proper classification of alcoholic beverages and glasses; proper mixing procedures on several cocktails and the uses and maintenance of different bar tools and equipment. - Direct observation of student providing advice to customers or colleagues on cocktail and its proper serving procedures.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice, exercises or essay questions
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Quizzes will test for knowledge of subjects in the chapter assigned for that day.
assessments.Note: These quizzes will be given at various times during class (beginning, middle or end). Total number of quizzes: 2

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice . Other types of questions may be included.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: The questions/ exercises will cover the lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and textbook.
assessments.Note: Not allow to use any document/information in any form in exam room
